name: Amynteo

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 4°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
